adjudicated.title: Multitenant Cybersecurity Operations Center Designed as an Open Cloud Service with Machine Learning Elements
adjudicated.venue_resolved: 2025 38th Conference of Open Innovations Association (FRUCT), Helsinki, Finland, 5-7 Nov 2025; publisher IEEE (DOI prefix 10.23919, proceedings-article, pp. 58-63); open-access full text on the association catalog at fruct.org (proceedings ISSN 2305-7254 print / 2343-0737 online), CC BY-ND per the catalog page.
adjudicated.reason: E3 confirmed at full text. The paper self-describes its method as a parametric literature review (WoS, "Elastic Stack/ELK/OpenSearch" + security keywords, 33 hits screened, 13 retained) and states that those 13 publications "form the sole evidence base for this article." The full text contains no original design artifact: no proposed-architecture figure of the authors' own, no implementation, no testbed, no deployment, and no measurement performed by the authors. The architecture-level content the second screen saw in the abstract (the recurring ELK-on-Kubernetes + optional Kafka/Spark foundation, the placement and trade-off tables) is a distillation of the 13 cited primaries, and the title's "Designed as" is aspirational framing for synthesis-derived design implications, which is exactly the survey-without-own-architecture-content case E3 excludes. Independently, I3 fails on first-party evidence: the comparison tables are a design aid built from secondhand results, not a substantive design evaluation the paper performed, and every quantitative figure in the text belongs to a cited primary. Under the Stream4Flow consistency bar (every cited number verified at the primary full text), nothing here is citable except by going around this paper to its references, several of which the review's own search reaches directly.
adjudicated.venue_integrity: Venue is legitimate and is not the governing factor. Crossref resolves the DOI to IEEE as publisher with the event record (Helsinki, 5-7 Nov 2025) matching the proceedings; the FRUCT series is long-running (38 editions since 2007, Finnish-origin open-innovations association), publishes to IEEE Xplore, maintains its own open-access catalog with registered ISSNs, and is indexed at the series level in dblp (the Nov-2025 volume not yet posted there at check time, consistent with normal indexing lag). Web checks surfaced no predatory, hijacking, or delisting flags for FRUCT. It is a regional non-flagship venue whose per-paper review depth I could not independently confirm beyond the Xplore-inclusion baseline, which would have mattered for tiering had the paper been topically eligible, but the exclusion rests on E3/I3, not on venue.
adjudicated.claim_check: Full text retrieved from the FRUCT open-access catalog (fruct.org/files/publications/volume-38/fruct38/Gab.pdf) and read in full (6 pages); DOI, venue, pagination, and authorship verified against the Crossref API record. The paper carries no first-party quantitative claims to verify — every figure traces to one of its 15 references. I traced the one prominent number (92 days / 2,750,654 connection attempts) to its stated source, Kyriakou & Sklavos, "Container-Based Honeypot Deployment for the Analysis of Malicious Activity," GIIS 2018, IEEE, DOI 10.1109/GIIS.2018.8635778, confirmed as a real IEEE publication, but its full text is paywalled so the figure could not be verified at the primary — which is itself the citability problem: any number lifted from this survey would be secondhand and unverifiable through it, failing the per-item verification bar the corpus applies (the Stream4Flow precedent). dblp does not yet index the paper (0 hits), consistent with the volume's Nov-2025 recency.

adjudicated.title: Federated Security Control Data Fabric: Scalable Telemetry Normalization and Orchestration in Multi-Cloud Environments
adjudicated.venue_resolved: International Journal of Computational and Experimental Science and Engineering (IJCESEN), ISSN 2149-9144, Vol. 11 No. 4 (2025) pp. 9295-9301; publisher of record at Crossref: "Iskender AKKURT" (individual, Süleyman Demirel University, Isparta, Turkey); DOI prefix 10.22399
adjudicated.reason: I3 fails at the full text, by the paper's own words. The second screen's hypothesis was that the full text might carry a substantive design evaluation the abstract omitted, but the Introduction states outright: "This work is primarily architectural and conceptual; it synthesizes existing technologies into a unified design pattern rather than presenting empirical benchmarks," and the Conclusions defer reference implementations, benchmark datasets, and quantitative evaluation to future work. There is no measurement, no benchmark, no deployment, and no evaluation section — the four tables are qualitative assertion grids, the "Implementation Feasibility" section is a recitation that OpenTelemetry/Iceberg/Delta/OCSF exist, and the paper contains not a single number of its own. Venue integrity independently disqualifies it even if I3 were argued: IJCESEN's publisher of record at Crossref is an individual person ("Iskender AKKURT"), the journal is absent from DOAJ, its output exploded 56→501→1,050 papers across 2023→2025 (the canonical capture curve), convergent secondary sources report Scopus discontinued it in the October 2025 list while the journal still advertises "indexed by SCOPUS," and this paper went submission-to-acceptance in two months at a venue publishing ~1,000 papers/year — the same dropped_predatory_or_compromised profile that sank 8 of the prior 14 refusals. Consistency with the Stream4Flow bar (every cited number verified at source) is unreachable here because there are no numbers to verify.
adjudicated.venue_integrity: Fails on multiple independent primaries. Crossref lists the publisher as a private individual, not an organization. DOAJ API returns zero results for ISSN 2149-9144. OpenAlex (S4210187448) shows is_core=false, hosts the journal under the "Turkish Online Journal of Qualitative Inquiry (TOJQI)" lineage — a title with documented clone/hijack history — and records the output explosion: 56 works in 2023, 501 in 2024, 1,050 in 2025, 267 by mid-2026, a ~20x expansion in two years. The journal was in Scopus (sourceid 21101210635; a Scimago page exists), and convergent secondaries (PhDTalks discontinued-list commentary; AskBisht journal profile) report Scopus discontinued it in the October 2025 update — I could not reach the official Elsevier discontinued-titles xlsx or the Scopus preview page from this environment (Cloudflare/403), so discontinuation is verified from secondaries, not the Elsevier primary, and I flag that honestly — while ijcesen.com still claims "IJCESEN is indexed by SCOPUS - TR Dizin," a misleading-indexing marker. Peer-review reality for this paper: received 2025-09-29, accepted 2025-11-29, published 2025-12-03, single "Independent Researcher, USA" author with a gmail contact, 10 references of which several are non-scholarly (Flexera blog, Gartner press release, Zscaler marketing report, two ResearchGate uploads, WJARR and IJSET papers), plus template-artifact author statements (plural "authors declare... equal right" on a single-author paper; a data-availability statement citing privacy restrictions for a paper with no data). Zero citations to date.
adjudicated.claim_check: The full text contains no quantitative claims of its own to verify — no throughput, latency, cost, or accuracy figures anywhere, only directional adjectives ("dramatically reduces storage costs," "substantially reduce network overhead") attributed to third-party citations. The only numbers referenced are background statistics from the Flexera 2024 State of the Cloud report and a 2022 Gartner ~$600B cloud-spend press release, cited as market context rather than findings. Table citation integrity is poor: e.g. Table 1 cites [3] (a federated-serverless review) and [4] (a 2013 event-processing paper) for generic egress-cost and volume-growth claims neither source establishes. Under the Stream4Flow standard — admit only after every cited number is verified at the full text — there is nothing here to verify, which is itself the I3 failure.

adjudicated.title: A Scalable AI-Enhanced Framework for Real-Time Streaming Analytics in High-Velocity Distributed Data Environments
adjudicated.venue_resolved: 2026 International Seminar on Intelligent Business and Edge-Computing Research (ISIBER) — inaugural edition, Universitas Siber Asia (UNSIA), Jakarta, Indonesia, 26 Feb 2026, hybrid one-day seminar; proceedings IEEE, pp. 31-36; resolved via Crossref for DOI 10.1109/ISIBER68248.2026.11470489
adjudicated.reason: E2 stands unrebutted, and venue integrity independently refuses the record. The second screen's admission condition was explicit — whether the Flink/Spark-Streaming/Kafka-Streams benchmark actually runs on security data is the full-text question — but the full text is unretrievable (IEEE Xplore paywall, no OA copy via Unpaywall/Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex, no preprint), and the abstract shows cybersecurity only as a named application domain alongside finance and social media, with no security-telemetry workload demonstrated, so the original E2 exclusion cannot be overturned at the retrievable depth. Even if full text later showed a security workload, the venue fails integrity outright: ISIBER 2026 is a first-edition one-day pay-to-present seminar that accepted ~180 papers for a single day — the conference-factory profile the review has refused 14 of 40 candidates over — and the abstract contains zero verifiable numbers, failing the Stream4Flow bar (every cited number verified at full text) by having no number to verify.
adjudicated.venue_integrity: Fails. Crossref confirms IEEE as publisher and the ISIBER 2026 event (Jakarta, 26 Feb 2026), so the DOI is real, but the venue profile matches the conference-factory pattern: an inaugural, single-day hybrid seminar hosted by an online university (UNSIA, "the 1st Cyber University in Indonesia") that by its own website received 586 submissions from 33 countries and accepted 30.72% (~180 papers) for one day of presentation — a review-and-presentation throughput a one-day seminar cannot genuinely deliver — with registration fees of $225-$300 and Xplore publication contingent on paid presentation, a claimed three-reviewer process that is unverifiable, a scope grab-bag in the same proceedings (financial-report ML, Roblox sentiment analysis, LLM inference batching, software-test optimization), and a "published in IEEE Xplore and Scopus" marketing claim I could not confirm from Scopus primaries. No predatory-list or delisting record exists, but the venue is five months old, so absence of a flag is not clearance. The paper's author block (one UIUC affiliation plus five "Independent Researcher, IEEE" entries, cited_by_count 0) matches the credential-publishing pattern, and the abstract's garbled prose ("produced most of the improvements in the time it took to process the data") reinforces the doubt about review reality. Peer review: claimed, not credible at the stated volume.
adjudicated.claim_check: No cited number could be verified at source because none exists at any retrievable depth: the abstract (retrieved independently from OpenAlex records.json and confirmed against the Semantic Scholar Graph API record, CorpusId 287545139) contains zero quantitative figures, and the full text behind the IEEE Xplore paywall has no open-access route — Semantic Scholar's openAccessPdf is empty, OpenAlex open_access_url is null, and web searches for a preprint or ResearchGate copy returned nothing. Crossref metadata (publisher, event, pages 31-36, six authors) was verified and matches the screened record, which also confirms the paper clears E4 on length (6 pages) — but with no verifiable number, the record fails the citability requirement on its own, independent of E2 and venue.

adjudicated.title: From Streams to Security: Architecting a Production-Ready Fraud Pipeline with Flink and Kafka (OpenAlex W7138965513)
adjudicated.venue_resolved: International Journal of Engineering Research & Technology (IJERT), ISSN 2278-0181, Vol. 15 Issue 03, March 2026, paper ID IJERTV15IS030725 — published as a Zenodo self-deposit (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19110590, DataCite-only; OpenAlex source type: repository, 'Zenodo (CERN)'; the E6 duplicate DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19110589 is the same deposit's second Zenodo DOI, mislabeled 'Open MIND' by OpenAlex). Author: Dhara Chimanbhai Trambadiya, Noble University, Junagadh, Gujarat, India. Full text: 8-page PDF retrieved from Zenodo.
adjudicated.reason: Venue integrity failure, which moots the topical question the second screen raised. On topicality the flag has merit — the pipeline architecture is itself the object of evaluation (E1 does not fire; the ML models are components, not the contribution), the streams include authentication logs with impossible-travel and velocity detections, and the authors frame it as real-time security analytics — so had the venue been sound, the E2 call could plausibly have been overturned at full text. But the venue is IJERT (ISSN 2278-0181), which fails every integrity check from primaries: named on the archived Beall's list of predatory standalone journals; absent from DOAJ (live API query, total 0); absent from Scopus/WoS; its own Crossref registration collapsed after 2020 (6,391 backfile DOIs, 0 current), after which it began minting DOIs by depositing PDFs to Zenodo — this paper's DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19110590 is a DataCite repository deposit, not a publisher DOI, and OpenAlex classifies its source as a repository. This repository's own prior appraisal rule (prisma-appraisal-2026-07-13.json, the dropped 'Open MIND' Zenodo deposit) is that a Zenodo DOI is a deposit, not a peer-reviewed venue, and the candidate's E6 duplicate W7138856164 carries that same 'Open MIND' OpenAlex mislabel. Peer-review reality is refuted by the full text itself: Section 3 ('System Architecture') opens with a paragraph copy-pasted from an unrelated Karachi Stock Exchange stock-price study (KSE-100 monthly prices Jan 2010–Dec 2014, SBP macro variables, Yahoo Finance) that no reviewer or editor caught, the reference list includes Medium blog posts, an '(unpublished)' entry, and journals I could not resolve to real venues ('Journal of Streaming Analytics', 'Indian Journal of FinTech Studies') — the two in-text citations carrying the introduction's load-bearing claims (Singh et al. 2025; Yasir et al. 2025) point to exactly those suspect venues — and Retraction Watch (2026-01-27) independently documents IJERT publishing a find-and-replace plagiarism ('grill' for 'broiler') with no listed editor-in-chief and silent removal rather than formal retraction. The headline evidence is also weaker than the abstract implies: the '94.2% sensitivity, sub-second, containerized deployment' is a single-machine Docker Compose simulation over 100,000 synthetic events in 30 minutes with Kafka replication factor 1 — simulation, not the production deployment the title claims. DUPLICATE DISPOSITION: the E6 duplicate W7138856164 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19110589, the same deposit's second Zenodo DOI, surfaced by OpenAlex under the 'Open MIND' repository mislabel) is the identical paper at the identical failed venue and resolves the same way — KEEP_EXCLUDED, E6 duplicate of an excluded record. Consistent with the 14-of-40 venue refusals and the Stream4Flow bar: this one does not clear.
adjudicated.venue_integrity: FAILS on every axis, all from primaries. (1) Predatory listing: IJERT appears by name on the archived Beall's list of standalone predatory journals (beallslist.net/standalone-journals). (2) Indexing: DOAJ live API query for issn:2278-0181 returns total 0; no Scopus or WoS coverage found; OpenAlex shows indexed_in ['datacite'] only. (3) DOI pattern: Crossref's journal record for 2278-0181 shows 6,391 backfile DOIs and 0 current DOIs with registrations collapsing after 2020 (2021: 30), i.e. the journal stopped registering publisher DOIs and now mints Zenodo repository DOIs — the structural self-deposit pattern this review's prior appraisal already ruled non-citable ('a Zenodo DOI is a DEPOSIT, not a peer-reviewed venue'). (4) Peer-review reality: refuted in-document — Section 3 opens with copy-paste from an unrelated stock-market paper; unresolvable/likely fabricated references carry the introduction's key claims; the journal self-describes as 'An International Peer-Reviewed Journal' on every page footer, published this paper the same day it was uploaded (2026-03-19), and Retraction Watch (2026-01-27, 'Engineering journal plucks poultry paper for plagiarism') documents IJERT's inadequate editorial oversight, no listed editor-in-chief, and silent-removal retraction handling. No retraction registered against this specific DOI (is_retracted: false), but the venue class is predatory/compromised, matching the 8 records previously dropped as dropped_predatory_or_compromised.
adjudicated.claim_check: All numbers the second screen quoted were verified present in the retrieved full text: '94.2% sensitivity' appears in the abstract and as TPR 94.2% in Table 1 and Section 5; 'sub-second response times' is substantiated in-text as 480 ms average / 780 ms p95; FPR 4.8% and 5,000 events/sec load also confirmed at source. So this is not a numbers-absent-from-source failure — the failure is that the numbers' provenance (synthetic single-node simulation) contradicts the deployment framing under which the abstract offers them, and the venue's absent peer review plus the in-document copy-paste contamination (unrelated KSE stock-market methodology text inside Section 3) mean no number from this paper can carry evidentiary weight in the review. Verification route: PDF downloaded from Zenodo record 19110590 (447.7 kB, 8 pages), text extracted and read in full; abstract cross-checked against the records.json entry, the Zenodo landing page, and the IJERT article page.

adjudicated.title: Real-Time Event Monitoring in Web Applications: An Optimized Architecture with AI-Driven Predictive Analytics
adjudicated.venue_resolved: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Processing, Hardware, Electronics, and Radio Systems (CIPHER), first edition, organized by the ECE Department, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar, India, 13-15 Feb 2026; IEEE conference proceedings (Crossref publisher IEEE, event record confirms name/location/dates); technically sponsored by IEEE Electron Devices Society per NIT Jalandhar's official announcement.
adjudicated.reason: Evidence not citable at the review's verification bar: the full text is closed on IEEE Xplore with no legal OA route (Unpaywall closed, no repository fulltext, no preprint), so the cybersecurity case study the second-screen flag ordered read cannot be read, and every number the review would cite (1.2M events/sec, 72% latency reduction, 75% faster security response, 92% anomaly accuracy) exists only in the abstract with method, baseline, and workload unknown — failing the every-number-verified-at-full-text bar that governed the Stream4Flow admission. Topical eligibility also stays unestablished: the second screen is right that E2 as literally worded ("no security application") doesn't cleanly hold since the abstract claims a cybersecurity case study, but I2 requires the paper's SUBJECT to be a data architecture handling security telemetry, and the abstract frames the subject as web-app user-behavior/reliability monitoring with security as one of two case-study domains and one of several potential applications; a 6-page first-edition-conference paper split across load testing plus two domains is unlikely (inference, unverifiable at abstract depth) to contain a substantive security-telemetry architecture evaluation. Bookkeeping note for the owner: the record's exclusion criterion would read more accurately as an I2 fail than E2, but the exclusion stands.
adjudicated.venue_integrity: Not predatory or hijacked: a real conference at a legitimate government engineering institute (NIT Jalandhar), IEEE-EDS technical sponsorship, proceedings genuinely in IEEE Xplore (DOI resolves; Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar concur on venue). But it is a FIRST-edition regional conference with no track record, its peer-review depth is unverifiable beyond IEEE's baseline Xplore inclusion bar, and this web-application data-engineering paper sits outside the conference's nominal electronics/hardware/radio-systems scope — a scope mismatch that suggests broad acceptance filtering and further weakens the peer-review-reality presumption. Paper has 15 references, 0 citations, indexed in Crossref only. Metadata trap recorded: OpenAlex maps the raw affiliation 'Axis Institute of Technology and Management, Kanpur' (a private teaching college) to IIT Kanpur; the raw Crossref affiliation string is authoritative. DOAJ not applicable (proceedings, not a journal); Scopus inclusion for this first-edition volume could not be confirmed from primaries.
adjudicated.claim_check: None of the cited numbers could be verified at source. Full text is paywalled on IEEE Xplore (page is JS-rendered and unfetchable; no institutional access in this environment) and no legal open copy exists: Unpaywall returns oa_status closed with best_oa_location null, Semantic Scholar has no openAccessPdf, OpenAlex reports any_repository_has_fulltext false with a single closed location, and targeted searches found no preprint, ResearchGate posting, or author copy. All five figures (1.2M events/sec, 72%, 30%, 75%, 92%) therefore rest solely on the abstract; the abstract text itself was cross-confirmed identical across OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, and the repo's records.json, but abstract self-report does not meet the review's per-item verification standard.

adjudicated.title: Geographic Access Audit Dashboard: Monitoring Oracle HCM Cloud Authentication Events via RESTful API Integration
adjudicated.venue_resolved: International Journal of Computational and Experimental Science and Engineering (IJCESEN), ISSN 2149-9144, Vol. 11 No. 4 (2025), pp. 8382-8389; DOI prefix 10.22399; Crossref publisher of record: "Iskender AKKURT" (individual, Crossref member 9684, also founder-editor-in-chief); OpenAlex host organization: Turkish Online Journal of Qualitative Inquiry (TOJQI); OJS site at ijcesen.com hosted by OJSDergi.com, Turkey.
adjudicated.reason: Venue integrity failure (predatory/compromised-pattern journal), with the original I3 exclusion independently confirmed on full text. The venue bundle is decisive on its own under the appraisal method's "dropped regardless of topical relevance" rule: IJCESEN's Crossref publisher of record for this DOI is an individual person, "Iskender AKKURT" (Crossref member 9684), who is also the journal's founder-editor-in-chief, so this is a one-person operation rather than an institutional publisher; OpenAlex resolves its host organization to "Turkish Online Journal of Qualitative Inquiry (TOJQI)", the imprint of a journal notorious for paper-mill capture; annual output exploded from 19-56 articles (2021-2023) to 501 (2024) and 1,050 (2025), with this article paginated 8382-8389 in a single volume year; the journal is absent from DOAJ (API: total 0) despite a decade as a fully-OA title; secondary sources report Scopus discontinued it in the October 2025 list while the journal's own site still claims Scopus indexing; and this paper went received-to-accepted in 5.5 weeks at a venue publishing roughly 20 papers/week, which is not compatible with real peer review. On the second screen's I3 question, the full text settles it against admission: the "detailed two-tier extraction spec" is generic prose (count endpoint, then paginate) with no endpoints, code, schemas, or figures, and the "middleware comparison" is three qualitative paragraphs comparing Oracle Integration Cloud against SOAPUI and Postman, which are API testing tools rather than middleware alternatives, so it is a strawman comparison, not a substantive design evaluation. The paper reports no measurement, no benchmark, no named or even anonymized production deployment, and not a single number anywhere, so there is nothing citable, and content tells (COBIT 2019 misattributed to "Zhang Xiaolu" at a random aliyuncs.com object-storage URL; "authors declare they have equal right" boilerplate on a single-author paper; author affiliation MSG Entertainment Holdings with no connection to the subject) corroborate negligible editorial review. Consistent with the corpus's prior handling: 8 of the 40 appraised were dropped predatory_or_compromised on comparable bundles, and the two sibling IJCESEN records in this search (ijcesen.4414, ijcesen.3715) were likewise excluded I3 for the same quantitative-free pattern.
adjudicated.venue_integrity: FAILS. Not in DOAJ (DOAJ API primary: 0 results for ISSN 2149-9144). Not an institutional publisher: Crossref registers the DOI under the founder-editor personally, and OpenAlex ties the journal to the TOJQI imprint, a documented paper-mill-captured title. Output pattern is mill-scale: OpenAlex counts_by_year show 12-56 works/year through 2023, then 501 (2024), 1,050 (2025), 267 (H1 2026), with volume pagination past 8,300 pages. Scopus: reported discontinued in the October 2025 delisting round (PhDTalks; not yet confirmable at an Elsevier primary because scopus.com and SCImago block unauthenticated access with 403/307), while the journal's own About page still claims "SCOPUS - TR Dizin" indexing, a claim-vs-reality gap that is itself a red flag. Peer-review reality: received 2025-09-22, accepted 2025-11-01, published 2025-11-04 at a venue running ~20 papers/week, with fabricated-looking references surviving review (COBIT 2019 attributed to "Zhang Xiaolu" via an aliyuncs.com bucket link; a 2009 OAM 10g developer guide cited for the REST audit API) and single-author boilerplate ("authors... equal right"). Scope collapse: a US entertainment-company employee's Oracle HCM HR-audit tutorial in a "computational and experimental science" journal. This matches the dropped_predatory_or_compromised class the appraisal has already refused 8 records under.
adjudicated.claim_check: The review would have no numbers to cite: the paper makes no quantitative claims in abstract or body (the abstract's "optimizes bandwidth utilization and processing efficiency" is attached to no figure in the full text, confirming the original I3 screen's reading). What was verified instead: the full PDF was retrieved and read end-to-end (ijcesen.com OA download, 8 pages, matching DOI 10.22399/ijcesen.4230 and the recorded pagination); Crossref API confirmed publisher-of-record "Iskender AKKURT", vol/issue, and the 2025-11-04/05 issue-and-registration dates; OpenAlex source API supplied the per-year output counts (501/1050/267 for 2024/2025/H1-2026); DOAJ's API returned zero journals for the ISSN; the journal's own About page was checked for its still-standing Scopus claim; and the paper's reference [10] (COBIT/"Zhang Xiaolu"/aliyuncs.com) and reference [5] (OAM 10g, 2009) were inspected in the PDF as review-quality evidence. The Scopus delisting could not be confirmed at an Elsevier primary (auth-walled) and is reported as secondary-sourced; the verdict does not depend on it.
